newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish jobless total around 248,000 in May-minister.
newsitem.headline: Irish jobless total around 248,000 in May-minister.

text.p: Irish government minister Proinsias de Rossa said on Tuesday that the number of people claiming unemployment benefit in Ireland fell to around 248,000 in May compared with 255,463 in April, Ireland's RTE broadcasting network said.
The official May figures for those claiming unemployment benefit are not due until Friday, but de Rossa said they would show a drop of around 7,000 compared to the April figure, RTE said.

De Rossa, minister for social welfare in Ireland's ruling "rainbow coalition", said the breach of the 250,000 barrier was an important milestone which demonstrated the success of the government's economic policies.
He said it was the first time in six years that the figure had been below 250,000.

Ireland goes to the polls on Friday. The ruling coalition of Prime Minister John Bruton has put job creation at the forefront of its election campaign and says it has created 1,000 jobs a week for the last two years.
